classification.difficultyReason: Construct symbolic proofs by combining equal base angles, triangle angle sum and supplementary angles.

spec.description: Downward-pointing isosceles triangle PQR with the horizontal side PR extended through R to S. Matching single ticks identify PQ and QR. The exterior angle QRS is marked a.
spec.mathematics: PQ=QR; P, R and S are collinear, with R between P and S; angle QRS has degree measure a. Coordinates reconstruct source proportions without asserting numerical side lengths.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens are visible. No proof steps or derived angles appear in the question diagram.

answer.short: $\angle PQR=(2a-180)^\circ$. The base angles are each $(180-a)^\circ$; subtract their sum from $180^\circ$.

inlines.text: Angles on a straight line sum to 180°.
Base angles of an isosceles triangle are equal.
Angles in a triangle sum to 180°.

spec.description: Downward-pointing isosceles triangle PQR with the horizontal side PR extended through R to S. Matching single ticks identify PQ and QR. The interior angle PQR is marked x.
spec.mathematics: PQ=QR; P, R and S are collinear, with R between P and S; angle PQR has degree measure x. Coordinates reconstruct source proportions without asserting numerical side lengths.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens are visible. No derived base angle or exterior angle appears in the question diagram.

answer.short: $\angle QRS=\left(90+\frac{x}{2}\right)^\circ$. Each base angle is $\left(\frac{180-x}{2}\right)^\circ$; subtract it from $180^\circ$.

inlines.text: Base angles of an isosceles triangle are equal, and angles in a triangle sum to 180°.
Angles on a straight line sum to 180°.
